operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole operative sentence says “I hereby revoke the said Executive Orders” Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823 so far as they pertain, respectively, to the three named organizations. The order states no effective date, so the partial revocation took effect when signed on October 10, 1949; the filing stamp reads October 11, 1949, disclosed as the alternative if effectiveness is tied to filing. The command was exhausted by performance and the end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10083 (14 FR 6161 (Federal Register of October 12, 1949)) was signed October 10, 1949. The filing stamp printed after the order reads October 11, 1949, one day after signing. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence beginning “NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 1 of the said International Organizations Immunities Act, I hereby revoke the said Executive Orders” and revoking those three orders only so far as they pertain to the three named organizations. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on October 10, 1949. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation. The Federal Register disposition-note search and the eCFR citation search report no hit naming this order. The packet's U.S. Code search entry also reports no hit, but the current-law table (jobs/current-law/output/ORDERS_CURRENT_LAW.csv) records one U.S. Code mention of this order (usc_mentions 1; MENTIONS.csv row usc:e410b86bce7b): the editorial note to 22 U.S.C. 288 headed 'Public International Organizations Formerly Entitled To Enjoy Certain Privileges, Exemptions, and Immunities' lists this order as the revoking order for the designations of the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees in the part of the note the held excerpt shows (the table counts three occurrences of the order's number). That note reports the revocation as completed, with the date and Federal Register citation of this order (October 10, 1949, 14 F.R. 6161), and neither restores, extends nor ends anything; it is consistent with the end date recorded here. The U.S. Code and eCFR searches test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Orders Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823, but only so far as they designated the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration, the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees as public international organizations remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists, because the only command in the order is the revocation itself and it was performed when the order took effect on October 10, 1949. The order states no effective date other than signing. The filing stamp printed after the order reads October 11, 1949, one day after signing. If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. No later instrument is claimed as an end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The order creates no independent continuing duty, board, fund or authority that could outlast it; whatever the revoked instrument itself provided is outside this order and is not claimed here.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Orders Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823, but only so far as they designated the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration, the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees as public international organizations stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked. Executive Orders 9698, 9751 and 9823 remain in force as to the other organizations they designate; they are independent instruments and are not claimed here.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence. The order revokes the three earlier orders only as to the three named organizations (its recitals say those organizations have ceased to exist or are in process of liquidation), so the earlier orders continue as to every other organization they designate; that continuation belongs to those earlier orders, not to this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Orders Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823, but only so far as they designated the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration, the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees as public international organizations stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked. Executive Orders 9698, 9751 and 9823 remain in force as to the other organizations they designate; they are independent instruments and are not claimed here.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10125 at 15 FR 2391 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 26, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 28, 1950 issue. Inventory corrected: one operative clause, offsets 1449 to the end of the sentence barring changes in conditions, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence. The dossier's span (offsets 672 to 3814) began at the order's heading and ran past the order's end, which comes at the words 'out of which the said dispute arose.' followed by the President's signature, into an unrelated Department of Agriculture regulation (Part 517, fresh apple export program, F.R. Doc. 50-3600) and the heading of Title 7 Part 201 (Federal Seed Act). The heading and the three recitals before the enacting words contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10125 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10125_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10125_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_d68f78cdf2.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated May 19, 1950 and a letter of transmittal to the President, signed by the board's chairman and two members (the text layer garbles the month in the letter's date line), which submits the board's report. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking May 19, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on May 19, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to June 18, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. research_rationale:
EO 10514 (signed 1954-01-19 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-01-20, 10:29 a.m.; 19 FR 369, Federal Register of January 21, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10514.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. The dossier split the order into a lead clause and a stray clause holding only the last year of the effective-date sentence; I replace them with one clause (characters 3415 to 3970 of the registered file), which holds the whole order: under the act of March 12, 1914 (38 Stat. 305) and on the Secretary of the Interior's recommendation, it revokes Executive Order 2414 of June 30, 1916 (hospital-service regulations for the construction and operation of the Government railway in Alaska, now the Alaska Railroad), and the order becomes effective at the close of business on December 31, 1953. First end: the revocation is a one-time act and was performed when the order was issued, so the clause was spent on signing, January 19, 1954; the filing date, January 20, 1954 (10:29 a.m.), is the alternative reading. The effective-date sentence makes the revocation of Executive Order 2414 effective retroactively at the close of business on December 31, 1953. That fixes when Executive Order 2414 is treated as ceasing; it cannot fix when this order's own command was performed, because this order did not exist on that date, so December 31, 1953 is the end of the revoked order and not of this one. The consequence, that Executive Order 2414 no longer applies, is a completed result and not a continuing command. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10514 found only the order's own copies, the earlier orders printed in the same issue and unrelated page numbers; none amends, postpones or revokes it. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Nothing held amends, postpones or revokes the order. Its first end is its issuance on signing, January 19, 1954; the filing date, January 20, 1954, is the alternative reading. The retroactive effective moment stated in the order, the close of business on December 31, 1953, is the date from which the revocation of Executive Order 2414 operates and precedes this order's existence, so it is not an end of this order.","independent_command_check":"The effective-date sentence only dates the revocation; the order contains no other command.","savings_check":"None stated; the revocation is a performed act with no continuing command.","scope_check":"One clause after correcting the dossier's split of the effective-date sentence; no partial effect is held or found."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order has no savings, exception or pending-matter wording. Its result, the revocation of Executive Order 2414 from the close of business on December 31, 1953, is a completed act with no continuing command.

BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES

A PROCLAMATION
WHEREAS Count Casimir Pulaski 
crossed the Atlantic to fight in the cause 
of freedom and gave his life for that 
cause on October 11, 1779, as a result of 
wounds received while leading the 
Pulaski Legion in a gallant cavalry 
charge at the siege of Savannah; and
WHEREAS the story of this Polish 
patriot’s supreme contribution to our 
independence is a treasured chapter in 
the annals of a grateful Nation; and
WHEREAS it is fitting that we should 
honor the memory of this distinguished 
soldier, who attained the rank of Briga­
dier General in the American Revolu­
tionary Army, on the one hundred and 
seventy-fifth anniversary of his heroic 
death:
NOW, THEREFORE, I, DW IGHT D. 
EISENHOWER, President of the United 
States of America, do hereby designate 
Monday, October 11, 1954, as General 
Pulaski’s Memorial Day, and I  invite the 
people of our country to observe the day 
with appropriate ceremonies. I  also di­
rect that the flag of the United States 
be displayed on all Government buildings 
on that day in tribute to General Casimir 
Pulaski.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I  have 
hereunto set my hand and caused the 
Seal of the United States of America to 
be affixed.

research_rationale:
EO 10563 (signed 1954-09-25 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-09-28, 2:14 p.m.; 19 FR 6297, Federal Register of September 30, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10563.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: one sentence, which under sections 301 and 426(c) of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947, as amended, revokes Executive Order 10266 of June 30, 1951 (suspension of certain provisions of that Act as they relate to officers of the Navy and Marine Corps). The order has no recital, effective-date wording, deadline or condition. First end: the revocation is a one-time act, so it was performed when the order took effect. With no effective-date wording the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1954-09-25; that reading is an inference from the signature block, and the filing date 1954-09-28 is the alternative. The consequence, that Executive Order 10266 no longer suspends the Act, is a completed result and not a command that continues. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10563 found only the order's own copies, the next order printed in the same issue (EO 10564) and unrelated page numbers; none amends or revokes it. Held EO 10365 (signed 1952-06-24), in paragraph 3, supersedes Executive Order No. 10266 of June 30, 1951 only so far as that order relates to the suspension of the operation of provisions of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947, as amended, for commissioned officers of the Marine Corps of the grades of captain and below. That partial supersession concerns the target of this order's revocation and not this order, so it is not an end of EO 10563; it is disclosed as an earlier event narrowing what the revocation accomplished, because the suspension in Executive Order 10266 continued for the Navy officers and for the Marine Corps grades above captain until this order revoked it. research_rationale:
EO:11704 (signed 1973-02-28; 38 FR 5619 (Federal Register of March 2, 1973)) is a single-command order. The order exempts A. Everette MacIntyre, a member of the Federal Trade Commission, from compulsory retirement for age under subsection (c) of section 8335 of title 5, United States Code, until February 28, 1974. The order recites that on February 1, 1972 the President issued Executive Order No. 11642 exempting him until February 28, 1973, and states that the public interest requires that he be further exempted. The surname is MacIntyre in both the register title and the held text; the given name is spelled Everett in the register title and Everette in the held text. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing in jobs/fr-originals; its number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: I confirm the dossier's one clause, which carries the recitals and the sole operative sentence; the text holds no other command, condition or proviso. The exemption ends by its own terms on 1974-02-28: the order's end date is quoted from the held text as "February 28,1974", recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, that it ends when February 28, 1974 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates). No later exemption of the same person is held: a name search of every held order text finds only EO 11568, EO 11642 and this order. Whether MacIntyre left office before the stated date is in no held source and is not asserted; the stated date is the latest day the exemption could operate. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all complete, none with a coverage warning): the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, citations of the order by number in statute text and notes; edition current through 2026-10-09) recorded 0 hits; the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML recorded 0 hits; the Federal Register catalog disposition-note search (1937 onward) recorded 0 hits for this order. I also searched every held order text (the Cruden held-text search, 33118 readable files) for the order's number; the only held text that cites it by number is its own Federal Register printing. EO 11568 (1970) and EO 11642 (1972) predate this order and do not cite it; they are found only by the person's name. A held-text search of the person's name finds only that person's own exemption orders (EO 11568, EO 11642 and EO 11704) and unrelated matches.

research_rationale:
EO 11767 of February 19, 1974 (39 FR 6603) consists of one operative paragraph designating the Organization of African Unity as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. Section 3 of EO 13377 of April 13, 2005 (70 FR 20263, published April 18, 2005) provides: "Executive Order 11767 of February 19, 1974, is revoked." The order has no own-terms sunset, condition or report date. Searches of the held corpus for the order's number found only EO 13377, the order's own texts, and an eCFR list (8 CFR 316.20) that still names the OAU designation; none revokes, supersedes or amends it earlier. The current-law table (jobs/current-law/output/ORDERS_CURRENT_LAW.csv) records one U.S. Code mention (MENTIONS.csv row usc:c26b8d90ee04, the editorial note to 22 U.S.C. 288) that lists the Organization of African Unity designation by Executive Order No. 11767 and says it was revoked by Executive Order No. 13377, section 3, April 13, 2005 (70 F.R. 20263), which agrees with the end recorded here, and one eCFR mention (8 CFR 316.20, amended through 2026-10-14) in a list of organizations that still names the Organization of African Unity with this order's date. That regulatory list makes no designation of its own and does not purport to restore the order, so it is not a current predicate for it; it is a stale list entry disclosed as a lead. The first and only dated end is the revocation on April 13, 2005.

20263Federal Register / Vol. 70, No. 73 / Monday, April 18, 2005 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 13377 of April 13, 2005
Designating the African Union as a Public International Or-
ganization Entitled To Enjoy Certain Privileges, Exemptions, 
and Immunities 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including sections 1 and 12 of the 
International Organizations Immunities Act (22 U.S.C. 288 and 288f–2), as 
amended by section 569(h) of the Foreign Operations, Export Financing, 
and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2005 (Division D of Public Law 
108–447), it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Designation. The African Union is hereby designated as a public 
international organization entitled to enjoy the privileges, exemptions, and 
immunities provided by the International Organizations Immunities Act. 
Sec. 2. Non-Abridgement. The designation in section 1 of this order is 
not intended to abridge in any respect privileges, exemptions, or immunities 
that the African Union otherwise may have acquired or may acquire by 
law. 
Sec. 3. Revocation. Executive Order 11767 of February 19, 1974, is revoked.
W

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12187, whose subject line describes providing for the base production control level for marginal properties. Sections 1-101 to 1-103 set, for pricing regulations under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 and for months commencing after December 31, 1979, the base production control level for marginal properties at 20 percent of the old crude oil produced and sold from the property in 1978 (divided by 365 and multiplied by the days in the month), define marginal properties by the crude oil pricing regulations, and let the Secretary of Energy adopt conforming regulations. Executive Order 12209 of April 16, 1980 restated the order to read as follows (before: the 20 percent level applied to months commencing after December 31, 1979; after: it applies only to the months of January, February and March 1980); under owner ruling 2026-10-21 that is a strike-and-insert rewrite, the clause continues, amended, and the substance changed. Fixed period of the restated section 1-101: Executive Order 12209, signed April 16, 1980, makes section 1-101 apply only with respect to the months of January, February and March 1980, and says it was issued to permit the conversion to new oil status of all old oil production from marginal oil wells effective April 1, 1980. That fixed period ended on March 31, 1980 (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins), before the restatement was signed, so the pricing rule has no application to any later month and the order was functionally spent as to that rule on March 31, 1980. The restatement itself took effect on signing, April 16, 1980 (no effective date is stated). This own-terms period is a disclosed earlier candidate end and is not adopted as the first end: the restatement leaves section 1-102 (the definition of marginal properties) and section 1-103 (the Secretary of Energy's power to adopt conforming regulations) in force without any date, the restated section 1-101 still fixes the base production control level for the covered months, and under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert rewrites the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, which here is the express revocation by Executive Order 12553. Whether the authority of the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 lapsed before 1986 is not established from held sources (the statute text is not held), and such a lapse would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only. Executive Order 12287 of January 28, 1981 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12287.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) exempted all crude oil and refined petroleum products from the price and allocation controls adopted under that Act without naming this order; it is likewise a disclosed candidate earlier end and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12209 of April 16, 1980
Base Production Control Level for Marginal Properties
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of 
the United States o f Am erica, including the Em ergency Petroleum A llocation 
A ct of 1973, as am ended (15 U.S.C. 751 e t  s e q .) , and notw ithstanding the 
delegations to the Secretary of Energy in Executive O rder No. 11790, as 
am ended by Executive Order No. 12038, and in order to permit the conversion 
to new  oil status o f all old oil production from m arginal oil w ells effective 
April 1,1980, it is hereby ordered that Executive O rder No. 12187 of D ecem ber 
29,1979, is am ended to read as follow s:
“1-101. For purposes o f the pricing regulations adopted pursuant to the 
Em ergency Petroleum A llocation A ct of 1973, w ith respect to the m onths of 
January, February and M arch 1980, the b ase production control level for 
marginal properties shall equal 20 percent of the total num ber of barrels of old 
crude oil produced and sold from the property concerned during calendar year 
1978, divided by 365, multiplied by the num ber of days during the month in 
1978 w hich corresponds to the months concerned.”
“1-102. For purposes of this Order, the term “m arginal properties” has the 
sam e meaning as that term under the crude oil pricing regulations adopted 
pursuant to the Em ergency Petroleum A llocation A ct of 1973, as am ended.”
“1-103. The Secretary of Energy may, pursuant to Executive Order No. 11790, 
as am ended by Executive Order No. 12038, adopt such regulations as he 
deems n ecessary  or appropriate to conform the crude oil pricing regulations to 
this Order.”.

Order.

Executive Order 12187 of December 29, 1979
Base Production Control Level for M arginal Properties
B y the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes o f 
the United States o f A m erica, including the Emergency Petroleum A llocation 
A c t o f 1973, as am ended (15 U .S .C . 751 e t se q.), and notwithstanding the 
delegations to the Secretary o f Energy in Executive Order N o. 11790, as 
am ended by Executive Order N o. 12038, and in order to delay the decontrol o f 
m arginal oil w ells, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. For purposes o f the pricing regulations adopted pursuant to the Emer­
gency Petroleum A llocation A c t o f 1973, with respect to months commencing 
after Decem ber 31, 1979, the base production control level for m arginal 
properties shall equal 20 percent o f the total number o f barrels o f old crude oil 
produced and sold from the property concerned during calendar year 1978, 
divided by 365, multiplied by the number o f days during the month in 1978 
w hich corresponds to the month concerned.

m eaning as that term under the crude oil pricing regulations adopted pursuant 
to the Emergency Petroleum A llocation A c t o f 1973, as am ended.
1-103. The Secretary o f Energy m ay, pursuant to Executive Order N o. 11790, as 
am ended by Executive Order N o. 12038, adopt such regulations as he deems 
necessary or appropriate to conform the crude oil pricing regulations to this 
Order.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12187 (45 FR 3, Federal Register of January 2, 1980; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Base Production Control Level for Marginal Properties and signed December 29, 1979. It sets the base production control level for marginal oil properties. Inventory: three numbered sections (1-101 to 1-103), recorded as one whole clause; the dossier inventory matches the full held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12187, whose subject line describes providing for the base production control level for marginal properties. Executive Order 12209 (1980-04-16) restated the order and is a later event, not an end. Fixed period of the restated section 1-101: Executive Order 12209, signed April 16, 1980, makes section 1-101 apply only with respect to the months of January, February and March 1980, and says it was issued to permit the conversion to new oil status of all old oil production from marginal oil wells effective April 1, 1980. That fixed period ended on March 31, 1980 (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins), before the restatement was signed, so the pricing rule has no application to any later month and the order was functionally spent as to that rule on March 31, 1980. The restatement itself took effect on signing, April 16, 1980 (no effective date is stated). This own-terms period is a disclosed earlier candidate end and is not adopted as the first end: the restatement leaves section 1-102 (the definition of marginal properties) and section 1-103 (the Secretary of Energy's power to adopt conforming regulations) in force without any date, the restated section 1-101 still fixes the base production control level for the covered months, and under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert rewrites the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, which here is the express revocation by Executive Order 12553. Title 3—
The President
Executive Order 12240 of September 26, 1980
Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution of the United 
States of America, and in order to provide for the extended life of the Nuclear 
Safety Oversight Committee to the extent that funds are to be made available 
therefor, it is hereby ordered as follows:
i-101. Section 1-303 of Executive Order No. 12202 is amended by adding 
thereto the following sentence: “Beginning O ctober 1,1980, such support shall 
be provided in accordance with Section 213 of the Independent Offices 
Appropriations Act, 1945 (31 U.S.C. 696).”.
1-102. Section 1-402 of Executive Order 12202 is amended to read, “The 
Committee shall terminate on September 30,1981.”.
1-103. In Section 1-102 of Executive Order No. 12202 the words “The member­
ship of the Committee shall be composed of five persons” is amended to read, 
“The membership of the Committee shall be composed of six persons.
THE WHITE HOUSE, 
Septem ber 26, 1980.
FR Doc. 80-30447 
Filed 9-26-80; 4:45 pm] 
Billing Code 3195-01-M

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: This clause is the order's enacting words and sections 1-1 to 1-3: the establishment of the Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee and its membership (1-101, 1-102), its advisory, reporting and agreement-making functions (1-201 to 1-211) and its staff, support, information and compensation provisions (1-301 to 1-305). Every command in it operates only through the Committee. First end: the order's own sunset as amended. Section 1-402 of the original text ended the Committee on September 30, 1980; Section 1-102 of EO 12240 (signed 1980-09-26, four days before that date) rewrote Section 1-402 to provide that the Committee shall "terminate on September 30,1981". The Committee therefore ended on 1981-09-30 by its own terms as amended (read inclusively, the Committee exists through that day; the exclusive reading would end it when September 30, 1981 begins, and the packet holds nothing that fixes the hour). Section 22 of EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17) and Section 4(c) of EO 12399 (effective 1982-12-31) revoke the order later, so they are later events, not the first end. The revocation is of the whole order by number and carves out no clause. Executive Order 12240 amended this clause before the end: section 1-101 of that order added to section 1-303 a sentence providing for support under section 213 of the Independent Offices Appropriations Act, 1945 from October 1, 1980, and section 1-103 of that order raised the membership in section 1-102 from five to six persons; the clause continues, amended, to the sunset. The sunset itself is in section 1-402, the second clause.

later_events.mechanism: amendments: Sec. 1-402 rewritten to a termination date of September 30, 1981 (before: September 30, 1980); Sec. 1-303 sentence added on support from October 1, 1980; Sec. 1-102 membership raised from five to six persons

research_rationale:
EO 12202 (Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee), signed 1980-03-18. The order establishes the Nuclear Safety Oversight Committee to advise on nuclear safety progress after the Three Mile Island accident (Sections 1-101, 1-102), sets its functions (1-2) and administrative provisions (1-3) and, in Section 1-402, its termination. EO 12240 (1980) extended the sunset by one year to September 30, 1981, raised membership from five to six and added a support sentence to Section 1-303. First end: the order's own sunset as amended. Section 1-402 of the original text ended the Committee on September 30, 1980; Section 1-102 of EO 12240 (signed 1980-09-26, four days before that date) rewrote Section 1-402 to provide that the Committee "terminate on September 30,1981". The Committee therefore ended on 1981-09-30 by its own terms as amended (read inclusively, the Committee exists through that day; the exclusive reading would end it when September 30, 1981 begins, and the packet holds nothing that fixes the hour). Section 22 of EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17) and Section 4(c) of EO 12399 (effective 1982-12-31) revoke the order later, so they are later events. Inventory corrected: the dossier's single clause (offsets 700 to 7081) stopped before section 1-4, so the held order text is covered by two clauses, the enacting words with sections 1-1 to 1-3 and section 1-4 (sections 1-401 and 1-402, which carries the sunset). research_rationale:
EO 12275 (Design Liaison Council), signed 1981-01-16. The order establishes an interagency Design Liaison Council (Sections 1-101 to 1-104: membership of listed agency heads, invited agencies, a chair from the Federal Council on the Arts and the Humanities, and other agencies that may be invited), defines design (Section 1-105) and directs the Council to encourage the exchange of information and research on design issues among federal agencies and to recommend changes in agency standards and procedures (Section 1-106). Inventory corrected: the dossier's single clause stopped before Sections 1-105 and 1-106, so two clauses now cover the whole held text. Its held text contains no sunset or termination provision. First end: Section 10 of EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, Termination of Boards, Committees, and Commissions) names this order by number, "Executive Order No. 12275," and provides that it is revoked. EO 12379 has no effective-date clause, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1982-08-17. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 1 establishes, effective July 10, 1982, a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. No earlier express end was found.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 2 directs the board to report within 30 days from the date of its creation. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The board's report is dated August 19, 1982 (held report of Emergency Board No. 194; the time was extended from August 9 to August 19, 1982 with the President's approval on July 26, 1982), so the command was functionally spent on August 19, 1982; that date is stated here and not entered as a later event because no dossier evidence record covers the transmittal letter or the extension passage. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 3 restates the section 10 status-quo period, from the date of creation of the board until 30 days after its report. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; it ran until thirty days after the report dated August 19, 1982, that is to about September 18, 1982 (a computed date, not shown in a source). No earlier express end was found.

certain railroads represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee  
of the National Railway Labor Conference designated on the list attached  
hereto and made a part hereof.
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens  
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a  
section of the country of essential transportation service.
NOW , THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by. Section 10 of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
Section 1. E s t a b lis h m e n t  o f  th e  B o a r d . There is established effective July 10,  
1982, a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate  
this dispute. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise  
interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
Sec. 2. R e p o r t. The board shall report its finding to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days from the date of its creation.
Sec. 3. M a in t a in in g  C o n d it io n s . A s provided by Section 10 of the Railway  
Labor Act, as amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board  
and for 30 days after the board has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be made by the carriers or by their  
employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12370 (47 FR 30047, Federal Register of July 12, 1982; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Certain Railroads Represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference and signed July 8, 1982. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and certain railroads represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 3 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (sec1; sec2; sec3). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; the held report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12370_Report_of_Presidential_Emergency_Board_No._194_created_by_EO_12370_effective_July_10__6dbdcaaa92.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) shows that the board's report and recommendations were submitted to the President by a letter of transmittal dated August 19, 1982 (the cover is also dated August 19, 1982), after the President approved on July 26, 1982 an extension of the time for the report from August 9, 1982 to August 19, 1982. The board therefore made its report on August 19, 1982, the report command was functionally spent on that date, and the thirty-day period after the report ran to about September 18, 1982 (a computed date, thirty days after the transmittal date, not a date shown in the source). These dates are stated here and not entered as later events because no dossier evidence record covers the transmittal letter or the extension passage (the dossier's records from that file quote other passages of the report). The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in an emergency-board report held under jobs/source-ladder. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12376, whose subject line describes increasing membership on the Presidential Commission on Drunk Driving. The single sentence amends the second sentence of section 1 of Executive Order 12358 of April 14, 1982 so that the Commission is composed of no more than 28 members appointed by the President (an increase of two). The amendment became part of the text of the parent order; the table of Executive Order 12553 lists this order by number and subject, so the revocation reaches it expressly, and no source shows the amendment being undone earlier. Executive Order 12415 of April 5, 1983 amended only section 4(b) of the parent order (the Commission’s termination date), not the membership sentence; it is a source note and not an end. The parent Commission's own termination date is a disclosed earlier candidate and not the first end: Executive Order 12415 of April 5, 1983 (48 FR 15117) amended section 4(b) of Executive Order No. 12358, as amended, to provide that the Commission shall terminate on December 31, 1983, and no held instrument extends it, so the Commission, and with it the membership ceiling this order set, had no operation after December 31, 1983 (functionally spent on that date on the inclusive reading). That instrument does not name Executive Order 12376, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments it is not an end; this order remained on the books until Executive Order 12553 revoked it by number. No earlier express end was found.

BILLING CODE 3410-02-M
7 CFR Part 917
Fresh Pears, Plums, and Peaches  
Grown in California; Nomination of  
Pear Commodity Committee Members
a g e n c y: Agricultural Marketing Service, 
USDA.
‘ACTION: Final rule.
s u m m a r y: This action reallocates the 
membership on the Pear Commodity 
Committee and re-groups districts (for 
purposes of representation) within the 
production area. The changes reflect the 
relative quantity of pears shipped from 
the respective representation areas.
d a t e : This rule becomes effective April
7,1983.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: 
William J. Doyle, Chief, Fruit Branch, 
F&V, AMS, USDA, Washington, D.C. 
20250, telephone 202-447-5975.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This 
final rule has been reviewed under 
Secretary’s Memorandum 1512-1 and 
Executive Order 12291 and has been 
designated a “non-major” rule. William
T. Manley, Deputy Administrator, 
Agricultural Marketing Service, has 
certified that this action will not have a 
significant economic impact on a 
substantial number of small entities. 
This action is designed to promote 
orderly marketing of fresh California 
pears for the benefit of producers, and 
will not substantially affect costs for the 
directly regulated handlers.
This final rule is issued under 
Marketing Order No. 917, regulating the 
handling of fresh pears, plums, and 
peaches grown in California. The order 
is effective under the Agricultural 
Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, as 
amended (7 U.S.C. 601-674). The action 
is based upon the recommendation and 
information submitted by the Pear 
Commodity Committee, and upon other 
available information. It is hereby found 
that this action will tend to effectuate 
the declared policy of the Act.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12393 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The four numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-104) establish, effective November 16, 1982, a three-member board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 159a), direct a report within 30 days after creation, restate the section 9A(c) status-quo period of 120 days after creation, and provide that the board terminates ninety days after the report. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; paragraph 1-103 measures it from the creation of the board, effective November 16, 1982, for 120 days thereafter, so by the order's own terms it ran out on March 16, 1983 (a computed date, 120 days after November 16, 1982), whatever the report date was. This clause provides that the board terminates on or after the submission of its report. The report date is not held in this packet’s citable evidence, and the clause is read as a report-relative sunset that is functionally spent on the report date and not as the end, by analogy to owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C), which that ruling applies to report-relative sunsets of other boards; this analogy is a reading disclosed for the reviewer. No earlier express end was found.

Title 3— Executive Order 12393 of November 16, 1982
The Presid en t Establishing an  E m erg en cy  B o ard  T o In vestigate a  D ispute  
B etw een  T he Long Island R ail R o ad  an d  C ertain  L ab or O rga­
nizations
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and certain labor  
organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a part hereof,  
representing employees of The Long Island Rail Road.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (“the Act”).
The New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the parent body of The  
Long Island Rail Road, has requested that the President establish an emergen­
cy board pursuant to Section 9A of the Act.
Section 9A(c) of the Act provides that the President, upon request of a party,  
shall appoint an emergency board to investigate and report on the dispute.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 9A of the Act,  
as amended (45 U.S.C. § 159a), it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Establishm ent o f Board.  There is established, effective November 16,  
1982, a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate  
this dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier. The board shall perform its  
functions subject to the availability of funds.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its findings to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days after the date of its creation.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions.  As provided by Section 9A(c) of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board, and for 120  
days thereafter, no change, except by agreement of the parties, shall be made  
by the carrier or the employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute  
arose.
1-104. Expiration.  The Emergency Board shall terminate ninety (90) days after  
the submission of the report provided for in paragraph 1-102 of this Order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12447, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government. The single sentence amends section 4(b) of Executive Order 12369, as amended, to read that the Committee (the President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government) terminates on December 31, 1983, unless sooner extended. The December 31, 1983 date never operated as an end: Executive Order 12455 of December 29, 1983 amended the same section 4(b) before that date (before: terminate on December 31, 1983; after: terminate on January 31, 1984, unless sooner extended); under owner ruling 2026-10-21 that is a strike-and-insert amendment, the clause continues, amended, and the substance (the termination date) changed. Executive Order 12534 of September 30, 1985 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12534.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) revokes the parent order 12369 but does not name this order; under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments) it is a disclosed candidate earlier end for the reviewer and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. The parent committee's amended termination date is a disclosed earlier candidate and not the first end: as further amended by Executive Order 12455 (signed December 29, 1983; 49 FR 345) section 4(b) of Executive Order No. 12369 provides that the Committee shall terminate on January 31, 1984, unless sooner extended, no held instrument extends it, and section 3 of Executive Order 12534 (signed September 30, 1985; 50 FR 40320, October 2, 1985) revokes Executive Order No. 12369 as one of the orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed. The Committee, and with it the termination date this order set, therefore had no operation after January 31, 1984 (functionally spent on that date on the inclusive reading; the recital in Executive Order 12534 does not say which of its three alternatives applies to this Committee). Neither instrument names Executive Order 12447, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments they are not ends; this order remained on the books until Executive Order 12553 revoked it by number. No earlier express end was found.

the Senior Executive Service.

monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 203(a)), the rates of basic allowances for

U.S.C. 403(a)) are adjusted, as set forth at Schedule 5 attached hereto and  
made a part hereof, for members of the uniformed services.

Act (Public Law 94-82, 89 Stat. 419) provides for adjustments in rates of pay  
and salaries as set forth at the schedules attached hereto and made a part

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12447 (48 FR 50055, Federal Register of October 31, 1983; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government and signed October 27, 1983. It extends the life of the President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government. Inventory: one amending sentence, confirmed against the full held text. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12447, whose subject line describes continuing the President’s Private Sector Survey on Cost Control in the Federal Government. Executive Order 12455 (1983-12-29) is a later event, not an end.  The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

(3) The parent committee's amended termination date is a disclosed earlier candidate and not the first end: as further amended by Executive Order 12455 (signed December 29, 1983; 49 FR 345) section 4(b) of Executive Order No. 12369 provides that the Committee shall terminate on January 31, 1984, unless sooner extended, no held instrument extends it, and section 3 of Executive Order 12534 (signed September 30, 1985; 50 FR 40320, October 2, 1985) revokes Executive Order No. 12369 as one of the orders that established committees that have terminated or been abolished by statute or whose work is completed. The Committee, and with it the termination date this order set, therefore had no operation after January 31, 1984 (functionally spent on that date on the inclusive reading; the recital in Executive Order 12534 does not say which of its three alternatives applies to this Committee). Neither instrument names Executive Order 12447, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments they are not ends; this order remained on the books until Executive Order 12553 revoked it by number. Executive Order 12554 of February 28, 1986
Nuclear Cooperation With EURATOM
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of  
the United States of America, including Section 162a(2) of the Atomic Energy  
Act of 1954, as amended (42 U.S.C. 2155(a)(2)), and having determined that,  
upon the expiration of the period specified in the first proviso to Section  
126a(2) of such Act and extended by Executive Orders No. 12193,12295,12351,  
12409, 12463, and 12506, failure to continue peaceful nuclear cooperation with  
the European Atomic Energy Community would be seriously prejudicial to the  
achievement of the United States non-proliferation objectives and would  
otherwise jeopardize the common defense and security of the United States,  
and having notified the Congress of this determination, I hereby extend the  
duration of that period to March 10,1987.
THE WHITE HOUSE,  
F e b r u a r y  28, 1986.
[FR Doc. 86-4791 
Filed 2-28-83; 3:59 pm] 
Billing code 3195-01-M

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order is a single determination and extension: having determined that failure to continue peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community would be seriously prejudicial to United States non-proliferation objectives, the President extends the duration of the period specified in the first proviso to Section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 to March 10, 1987. The extension therefore runs by its own terms to March 10, 1987, recorded inclusive (the period runs through that day; the exclusive reading ends it when March 10 begins). Executive Order No. 12587, signed March 9, 1987 before that date, extended the period to March 10, 1988 without revoking or superseding this order; that and the later annual extension orders (Executive Orders 12629, 12670, 12706, 12753, 12791, 12840 and 12903, whose texts are held) are later events, each of which recites this order in a list of earlier extensions. Executive Orders 12629, 12706, 12753, 12791, 12840 and 12903 each state that the immediately preceding extension order shall be superseded on the effective date of the new order (12629 supersedes 12587, 12706 supersedes 12670, 12753 supersedes 12706, 12791 supersedes 12753, 12840 supersedes 12791 and 12903 supersedes 12840); Executive Orders 12587 and 12670 contain no supersession sentence. None of them supersedes or revokes this order, so none is treated as ending it. The effective date of each later order is taken as its signing date because none states a different one.

research_rationale:
Identity confirmed against the census register (executive order of 1986-02-28, Nuclear Cooperation With EURATOM) and the held Federal Register text at 51 FR 7423, whose text layer shows the March 4, 1986 issue. The order has one operative sentence, an extension to a stated date, March 10, 1987, which is the first end by its own terms. The held texts of the later extension orders show a chain of annual extensions that recite this order; none revokes or supersedes it.
